about.title: Morgan Hill Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a traffic collision in Morgan Hill takes a family member, the aftermath is disorienting on top of devastating. Santa Clara County's recent traffic count included three deaths, and behind each number is a household now facing funeral arrangements, missing income, and unanswered questions. Corridors like Monterey Road, Dunne Avenue, Butterfield Boulevard, and the US-101 stretch through town see steady collision activity, particularly around Friday evening traffic. California wrongful death law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to pursue a civil claim separate from any police investigation or criminal case. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we're a free service that connects families with an independent attorney who handles these matters on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. If you're trying to understand whether you or your family qualifies to bring a claim, and what the two-year filing window means for your situation, we can help you get a conversation started with someone who knows this area of law well.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Morgan Hill Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Can Be Confusing
items.desc: California limits who can file a wrongful death claim, generally a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain cases. An attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies before time runs short.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Firm
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shortens considerably if a government entity, like a public roadway agency, may be responsible. Getting matched with an attorney early protects your ability to file.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance, losses that are real but not always considered right away. An attorney can help identify what applies to your family's situation.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify under certain circumstances. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to confirm who has standing.

items.question: Does the wrongful death case depend on whether police filed criminal charges?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal proceedings related to the same crash. Even if charges are never filed or a case is resolved differently in criminal court, a civil claim can still move forward independently.

items.question: Why does it matter that the crash happened on a road like Monterey Road or Dunne Avenue in Morgan Hill?
items.answer: Where a collision occurs can affect who might be responsible, especially if road design, signage, or maintenance played a role alongside driver conduct. It can also affect deadlines if a government agency maintains that roadway. An independent attorney can look at the specific location and circumstances to help you understand your options.

items.question: How much does it cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing upfront. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your family recovers compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
